$comment: First-party plugin registry (AGL-417). THE single place that maps plugin ids to packages, register entry points, and API path prefixes. `tools/scripts/generate-plugin-manifests.mjs` turns this into the per-app generated loader manifests — the only files allowed to reference @aglyn/plugins-* outside libs/plugins. `catalog` is the plugin's row on the workspace and site switchboards (label, description, release flag, what switching it off for a site stops, and what a published site loses); the generator compiles every row, in `order`, into libs/aglyn plugin-manager/first-party-plugins.generated.ts, so a new plugin is declared here and nowhere in core (AGL-3080). An entry with no `catalog` is not on the switchboard. `capabilities` are further switchboard ids the same bundle serves. `uses` lists the plugins whose contracts this one imports (AGL-3980): `@aglyn/plugins-<id>/contracts` and nothing else of them, an optional code dependency (the plugin still runs with them absent), carried as an optional peer in its package.json; `catalog.requires` is the hard kind, a plugin that cannot be switched on without another, and it allows the same import. `check:lib-boundaries` refuses any other import of one plugin by another. register keys: site = canvas/site components (client barrel), console = ConsoleExtension (client barrel), tenantApi/consoleApi = API handlers (/server entry), declarations = the light registrations core reads before any surface loads (`/declarations`, both apps, client and server), consoleDeclarations = the same for the CONSOLE alone, client and server (`/declarations.console`, never loaded or bundled by the tenant runtime: keys only the console reads, such as a console-only plugin's permission keys), serverDeclarations = the same for the server alone (`/declarations.server`, platform-event subscriptions), consoleServerDeclarations = the same for the CONSOLE's server alone (`/declarations.console-server`, never loaded or bundled by the tenant runtime: for registrations that open what only the console holds), subprocessors = the third-party recipients the plugin's code sends data to, and its other hosts and its uses of hosts declared elsewhere (`/subprocessors`, called by the generator rather than at runtime, and written into the console's subprocessors manifest as data for the subprocessor inventory), planEntitlements = what each plan includes of the plugin's own entitlement keys (`/plan-entitlements`, called by the generator rather than at runtime and compiled into the catalog file as data that core's PLAN_ENTITLEMENTS composes, because the pricing tables and the plan comparison read it without loading a plugin), usageAxes = the meters the plugin contributes to the platform's cost model and utilization table, and the lines of spend it adds to a workspace's usage budget (`/usage-axes`, called by the generator and compiled into the catalog file as data, because the discount guardrail and the staff org page price a rollup without loading a plugin), videoEmbedProviders = the video hosts whose own player the plugin's Video element frames (`/video-embed-providers`, called by the generator and compiled into the catalog file as data, which the published page and the tenant's frame-src read without loading the plugin), tenantEmails = the emails a site sends its own customers through the plugin (`/tenant-emails`, called by the generator and compiled into the email lib's tenant email catalog as data, which the send path reads without loading the plugin). activityMutationPaths = the plugin's modules that create, transfer or destroy a durable customer object, which `tools/scripts/check-activity-coverage.mjs` holds to logging an activity entry like the platform's own. `alwaysOn` here is the LOADER's meaning — the bundle activates whatever ids `ensure()` is given, so it defeats the per-page narrowing in required-site-plugins.ts and belongs only to `mui`, which the canvas cannot render without. A plugin that merely may not be switched OFF says so with `alwaysOn` in FIRST_PARTY_PLUGINS instead. `modules` (AGL-3116) names the subpath a surface registers from when that surface's code must not ride with the package root's — each site surface has its own module, so a published page never loads a console registrar. `contributes` (AGL-3116, required) declares what the plugin adds and where, in the shape a marketplace manifest uses (core `plugin-contributions.ts`): `site.components` = the canvas component ids it registers, `site.features` = the site runtimes it mounts on every page of a site that switched it on, `console.slots` = the widget slots and panels it fills, `console.routes` / `console.orgRoutes` = the console routes it serves, `console.shell` = it draws a nav tab, a provider or a staff tab the shell renders on every screen. The loaders place a plugin by this declaration alone, so `apps/console/specs/plugin-contributions-declared.spec.ts` holds it to what the registrars actually register. `hostCollections` (AGL-3080) = the subcollections under a site the plugin owns (core `plugin-host-collections.ts`); a collection's `resource` is the KIND a client creates a document in it as, through the platform's generic create route — its field allow-list, plan counter, feature and stamps (core `plugin-host-resources.ts`), compiled and never registered, because that route is a security path. A collection's `siteExport` is how the whole-site backup carries it and what a restore writes back (core `plugin-site-export.ts`). `sitemapSections` (AGL-3080) = the child sitemaps the plugin's own pages fill (core `plugin-sitemap-sections.ts`), compiled because the tenant's sitemap is a published-site reader. `sitemapReaders` (AGL-3475) = child-sitemap families a plugin's READER lists, for pages no single site collection describes (core `plugin-sitemap-readers.ts`): each `section` is a family whose children are `{section}-{key}`, compiled so an index cannot silently drop them, with the reader registered from `serverDeclarations`. `consoleRedirects` (AGL-3080) = the plugin's old console addresses and where each answers now, in Next's redirect shape, compiled into `apps/console/constants/plugins.redirects.generated.json`, which the console's next.config.js spreads into its redirects. `siteBundleSections` (AGL-3080) = the sections of the whole-site backup the plugin answers for itself, data a host collection's `siteExport` cannot describe (core `plugin-site-bundle.ts`): declared here, registered from `serverDeclarations`, and an export fails rather than leaving a declared section out. `transferResources` (AGL-3523) = what the plugin can import and export, each a `TransferResourceDescriptor` from core `data-transfer/resource.ts` (key, label, scope, kinds, formats, limits; core `plugin-transfer-resources.ts`): declared here, the server half registered from `serverDeclarations` or `consoleServerDeclarations`, the client half from the console registrar loaded at the `transferResources` slot, and a job fails rather than leaving a declared resource out. `taxReturnSource: true` (AGL-3080) = the plugin sells through the platform's own account and registers a tax return source (core `plugin-tax-return-sources.ts`); the operator's sales tax return refuses to be filed while a declared source is unregistered. `revenueSource: true` (AGL-3080) = the plugin earns the operator a take through the platform's account and registers a revenue source (core `plugin-revenue-sources.ts`); the staff revenue report names a declared source it could not read rather than counting it as zero. `notificationCategories` (AGL-3080) = the preference buckets the plugin's notification types fall in, by the prefix before the dot: an `id` no other plugin and not the core owns, a `label` and `description` for the settings page, and `defaults` for the console and email channels; compiled into the catalog file and read by core `notifications.ts`, because the fan-out resolves channels in processes that load no plugin. The id keys stored preferences, so it is never renamed. `notificationDigests` (AGL-3080) = the digests the plugin sends on its own schedule: the `key` its on-by-default switch is stored under in `users/{uid}.digestPrefs`, and the switch's `label` and `description`, compiled the same way so the settings page draws it without loading the plugin. `interactionSteps` (AGL-3080) = the steps the plugin adds to interactions: the stored `type`, the `label` editors, run histories and drafters name it by, and for a step that acts on one of the plugin's records, `picks` — the site collection it lists them from (one the plugin declares under `hostCollections`), the step fields holding the pick, and the words for the picker and for a step with none. `offered: false` keeps a step only an automation holds out of the besigner's interaction builder; `holds` marks a step that suspends the run, with the band of whole minutes it may hold and the `timeoutField` a hold that ran out of time leaves in scope, and a visitor's page never runs a step past one; `typedFields` are the fields a person types words into, each with the words a sentence `names` it by, where a drafted step may leave a bracketed placeholder. Compiled into the catalog file and read by core `site-interactions.ts` and `draft-placeholders.ts`. `hostEvents` (AGL-3080) = the host events the plugin's server doors raise with `emitHostEvent`: the `type` an automation's trigger stores (never renamed), its `order` in every trigger picker (the platform's own `pageView` is 20), the `label` pickers and run rows show, and the `payloadKeys` it puts in scope; compiled into `app-utils/plugin-host-events.generated.ts` and read by core `host-events.ts`, because the event bus, the trigger pickers and the validators read them with no plugin loaded. `containers` (AGL-3080) = the container kinds the plugin keeps — a document other records are filed under by naming its id in `<kind>Ids` on their own document, a campaign being the first — with the org collection a picker reads them from; compiled into core `plugin-manager/plugin-containers.generated.ts`, which the membership helpers and the container picker read. `mobile` (AGL-3620) = the plugin's surface in the Aglyn mobile apps: `register` names the registrar its `./mobile` entry (`src/mobile/index.ts`, never re-exported from a web entry) exports, and `contributes` lists the ids it registers by kind (`screens`, `tabs`, `widgets`, `quickActions`, `deepLinks`); the generator compiles them into the SEPARATE `apps/mobile/src/plugins.mobile.generated.ts`, the only manifest a mobile app reads, so the web manifests never change for it, and the app's loader refuses a registration the declaration does not name. `subscriptionTopics` (AGL-3080) = the streams the plugin's mail is sent under, which a recipient can leave one at a time (`id` is a wire value: it rides in every signed unsubscribe link and keys every recorded opt-out, so it is never renamed), in the preference page's `order`; exactly one plugin marks its topic `default`, the stream a campaign or a scheduled automated email belongs to when it names none. Compiled into core `plugin-manager/plugin-subscription-topics.generated.ts`, the built-in floor of every org's topic catalog.

catalog.description: Products, carts, checkout, orders, POS.

releaseFlagDefinition.description: Full ecommerce wave: catalog/variants, cart + checkout, digital goods, reservations, POS, and the repriced commerce tiers (AGL-276..331).

resource.label: products
resource.$comment: The whole product model: the editor, the duplicate action and the CSV importer each send a full product. `nameLower`, `nameTokens`, `nameReversed`, `skus`, `barcodes`, `priceFromCents`, `soldOut` and `collectionIds` are the search, price, stock and smart-collection keys this plugin derives on the payload (`productSearchFields`, `productStockFields`, `productCollectionIds`; AGL-2501, AGL-3321), so they are allow-listed rather than stamped. `priceUsd`, `inventory` and `imageUrl` are the legacy Commerce Starter fields every caller still writes. Born live — `deletedAt: null` — because the products table queries `deletedAt == null` and Firestore cannot match an absent field; a duplicate never carries its source's soft delete.

hostCollections.name: siteMemberCredentials
hostCollections.mediaScanReason: A site member's password hash, one document per member, read and written only by the membership routes (AGL-3308). A credential with no content field, and no client may read it.

hostCollections.name: orders
hostCollections.mediaScanReason: Completed orders. Line items COPY a product's `imageUrl` at purchase time, so these would match — and matching would be the wrong answer: an order is an immutable record of what was sold, deleting the asset changes nothing about it, and no author can edit one. A busy store also holds more of these than the whole read budget.

hostCollections.name: carts
hostCollections.mediaScanReason: Live and abandoned carts, with the same copied line-item image and the same reasoning, at higher volume — one document per shopper session.

hostCollections.name: checkouts
hostCollections.mediaScanReason: In-flight checkout sessions. Transient buyer state carrying the same line-item snapshot as `carts`.

hostCollections.name: reservations
hostCollections.mediaScanReason: POS and booking holds. Short-lived transaction rows pointing at a resource that is itself scanned.

hostCollections.name: stockHolds
hostCollections.mediaScanReason: Inventory holds taken during checkout. Machine-written, short-lived, and a quantity rather than content.

hostCollections.name: subscriptions
hostCollections.mediaScanReason: Site membership subscriptions: a plan pointer, a status and Stripe ids. Server-written from the billing webhook.

hostCollections.name: registers
hostCollections.mediaScanReason: POS register allocations — a count against the register add-on, read by billing (AGL-1775). No content field at all.

resource.label: POS registers
resource.$comment: The count is met against the site's allocation of the org's register seats (AGL-1775), which the platform resolves from this quota key; `pos` gates POS at all.

hostCollections.name: giftCards
hostCollections.mediaScanReason: Gift card balances and redemption history. Money, not content.

hostCollections.name: licenseKeys
hostCollections.mediaScanReason: Digital-product license keys issued at fulfilment: a code, an order pointer and a revocation flag.

hostCollections.name: inventoryAdjustments
hostCollections.mediaScanReason: The append-only stock adjustment ledger (AGL-2269). One row per manual stock edit and per cancellation release, unbounded over a store's life.

hostCollections.name: inventoryReconciliation
hostCollections.mediaScanReason: Reconciliation runs comparing counted stock against recorded stock. Machine-written totals.

hostCollections.name: restockAlerts
hostCollections.mediaScanReason: Back-in-stock requests: an email address and a product pointer, written by visitors.

hostCollections.name: stripeTaxRates
hostCollections.mediaScanReason: Cached Stripe tax rate ids, written by the tax sync. Vendor ids.

hostCollections.name: returns
hostCollections.mediaScanReason: Returns (AGL-3611): line indexes, quantities, reasons and a return label link, written only by the returns routes. A return names no image of its own; the order's lines carry the copies, and the order is not scanned for the same reason.

hostCollections.name: orderWebhooks
hostCollections.mediaScanReason: The merchant's outbound order webhook endpoints (AGL-3611): a URL and the event names it takes. Scanning reads every endpoint for a URL that is never a media file.

hostCollections.name: orderWebhookSecrets
hostCollections.mediaScanReason: Sealed HMAC signing secrets for the order webhooks (AGL-3611). Reading them for media would put a secret on a scan path to match nothing.

hostCollections.name: orderWebhookDeliveries
hostCollections.mediaScanReason: The webhook delivery log (AGL-3611): one row per event per endpoint, expiring after 30 days. A body copies the order, whose image URLs record what was sold rather than use the file, so a match would be wrong, and a busy store holds thousands.

hostCollections.name: posStaffPins
hostCollections.mediaScanReason: Register staff PINs (AGL-3609): a salted hash and a lockout counter per member, written only by the staff PIN route. No content field at all.

hostCollections.name: posOfflineSales
hostCollections.mediaScanReason: The offline register's sync records (AGL-3625): one per cash sale rung offline, holding its order id, flags and stock conflicts, written only by the sync route. No content field, and a busy offline register writes one per sale.

hostCollections.name: checkIns
hostCollections.mediaScanReason: Who is due at the check-in window on a day and who checked them in (AGL-4043): a customer's name and contact details, an item name, a status and a wristband, written only by the check-in route. No content field, and a busy day writes one per person.

hostCollections.name: checkInDays
hostCollections.mediaScanReason: When each day's check-ins were last brought in line with its orders and stays (AGL-4043): a time and a flag, written only by the check-in route.

hostCollections.name: terminal
hostCollections.mediaScanReason: The site's Stripe Terminal Location (AGL-3607): a vendor id and the address it was registered with, written only by the reader routes. No content field.

hostCollections.name: terminalReaders
hostCollections.mediaScanReason: The site's card readers (AGL-3607): a Stripe reader id, a label and a status, written only by `/api/commerce/pos-readers`. No content field.

hostCollections.name: printers
hostCollections.mediaScanReason: Cloud receipt printers (AGL-3619): a device id, a secret version, a paper width and a status. A receipt logo is the one stored IN the printer and named by a key code, never a file URL, so nothing here can use an asset.

hostCollections.name: printJobs
hostCollections.mediaScanReason: The printers' queue (AGL-3619): rendered receipt, ticket and label bytes waiting for a printer's poll, written by the print routes and gone once printed. Printer commands, not content, and a busy register queues hundreds a day.

sitemapSections.$comment: A product page for each active product with a slug, once the store names the template products render through (AGL-299). Soft deletes keep `status: active`, hence skipWhen. Commerce stamps epoch milliseconds.
The catalog collections served at /collections/{slug} (AGL-954), once the store names their template. A content collection is the platform's own section.

hostEvents.$comment: Order and return events (AGL-3611): raised through the plugin event outbox and handed to the host event bus by commerce's own subscriber, so they reach an automation at least once and within a minute of the fact.

transferResources.description: Products with their options, variants, prices, stock, images and search listing.

A card's ID is its code. plugins.$comment: AGL-3700: Weglot translation for a merchant's published site, with the MERCHANT'S OWN Weglot account and public project key (merchant-provided: Aglyn holds no Weglot account and no server of ours calls it). Off per site until a site admin switches it on (`defaultOffPerSite`); settings are the platform's generic plugin settings (`pluginSettings/weglot`), drawn by the console's settings card from the schema `declarations` registers. The tenant enricher (`tenantApi`) writes the page slice only for a site that switched it on, on a plan with `multilingual`, with valid settings; the site runtime loads Weglot's script without blocking render. `siteIntegration` widens the site's connect-src/img-src to Weglot's exact hosts under the same three conditions (core `site-integrations.ts`). Client-side translation only: no hreflang and no Weglot subdomain/subdirectory mode are built.

siteOff.keeps: Your Weglot settings and your Weglot account's translations are kept.

siteCsp.$comment: The hosts Weglot's script reaches from the visitor's browser, read out of weglot.min.js 5.90.2 (libs/plugins/weglot/src/lib/constants.ts holds the same list). One variant: Weglot has no provider choice.

plugins.$comment: AGL-3716: the Music player element, playing the owner's OWN audio from the media library (or an external URL the author confirms they hold the rights to). Site surface only: the published page loads it where a page places a player. No third-party catalog, no download control, and a copyright takedown is the platform's media quarantine (reason `dmca`), which the CDN answers with a 410 and the player names as an unavailable track.

siteOff.keeps: The audio in your media library is kept, and players keep working on the workspace's other sites.

catalog.$comment: Buy a domain for a site and have it connected with no DNS step (AGL-3962), through a registrar driver (Vercel's Registrar API first), and point a domain the owner already holds here in one click through the Domain Connect standard (AGL-3963). On for every workspace and no release flag: buying hides itself until the deployment names a registrar and a Stripe product (DOMAINS_REGISTRAR, DOMAINS_STRIPE_PRODUCT_ID), and one-click DNS until it holds a signing key (DOMAIN_CONNECT_PRIVATE_KEY). Starter and up, through core's customDomain entitlement.

siteOff.keeps: Domains bought for this site stay registered to you and keep renewing until you turn auto-renew off or transfer them out, and Domains keeps working on the workspace’s other sites.
